extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, agencies, and marketing/communications specialists measuring PR campaign results
extracted.subtask_description: Practical how-to guidance for planning, tracking, and reporting public relations campaign results using media monitoring, social listening, and PR metrics. Includes which metrics to track, how to configure monitoring, and how to present results to stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning and goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish planning and goals before buying a media monitoring tool — ask: What kind of PR campaigns are you planning to run? What does success entail in these campaigns? Do you want to measure brand awareness, sentiment, or something entirely different?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose metrics appropriate to the ultimate goal of your PR campaign. Example: if the main goal is to measure sentiment after a product launch, set up measurement for sentiment alone. Test brand sentiment often to have a solid basis for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish vanity metrics vs quality metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the main distinction between vanity and quality metrics — vanity metrics don’t tell you much about actual performance but look good on paper, while quality metrics give tangible results that more accurately determine campaign performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of reporting only vanity metrics because C-suite/clients understand them, expect them, and they’re easy to generate — but they can misrepresent real impact. Prefer quality metrics aligned with campaign goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: AVE (Advertising Value Equivalent) — treat as a vanity metric
rubrics_metrics.description: AVE estimates the value of a PR mention by comparing it to the cost of a similar advertisement (e.g., assigning a quarter-page article the cost of that ad space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article calls AVE 'the flagship example of a vanity public relations metric' and notes it is outdated and no longer effective for modern PR. Learn when to use it and when to consider alternatives; avoid relying on AVE as a primary success measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: UVPM / Domain Reach (as a vanity/generic traffic metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: UVPM (Unique Visitors per Month), also called Domain Reach, measures the number of individuals who accessed a website in a month. Interpretation varies between PR and marketing teams and is described as 'rather generic.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize UVPM can be misleading for PR impact; consult alternatives and context-specific measures when assessing visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of mentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of media mentions of your tracked terms/brand across channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mentions as a basic indicator of activity and reach but pair with quality metrics (e.g., where mentions appear, sentiment, audience) to assess real impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated reach
rubrics_metrics.description: An estimate of how many people could have seen a given mention (used as a reach proxy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use estimated reach to prioritize mentions, but understand it's an estimate — combine with domain metrics and engagement measures for a fuller picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain reach / domain rank / domain authority score
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics describing the relative strength or traffic potential of websites where mentions appear (domain reach, domain rank, domain authority on a 0–99 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track domain authority to show how PR efforts contribute to SEO and to value backlinks; higher domain authority suggests more valuable backlinks. Domain rank/authority are machine-learning-derived proxies—use them to help non-SEO audiences understand value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of Voice (SoV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track organic, unpaid mentions of your brand across the web to see how your brand stacks up versus competitors in visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SoV to measure brand visibility changes over time and versus competitors; it is a recommended quality metric for brand awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media mentions (backbone metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tracking press hits and social media mentions across blogs, forums, review sites, and social platforms to see where and how target audiences talk about your brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specialist media monitoring tools to get real-time alerts about relevant media mentions. Filter and prioritize mentions that matter rather than collecting everything.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media tiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify mentions by media tiers (e.g., platform/channel importance) to determine whether you’re being mentioned on the right platforms for your audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set advanced filters to break down mentions across platforms and tiers so you can answer 'am I being mentioned on the right platforms?' and focus on channels where your audience is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top mentions (customizable)
rubrics_metrics.description: A leaderboard of 'top mentions' defined by whatever criteria you choose (e.g., industry relevance, domain rating).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define 'top' for your context (e.g., domain rating, audience relevance) and use top mentions to surface the most valuable coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure whether mentions are positive, neutral, or negative to understand public perception and track changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine automated sentiment analysis with human review (see separate guidance). Use sentiment tracking to monitor campaign effects and to trigger crisis responses if negative sentiment spikes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention backlinks / number of backlinks
rubrics_metrics.description: Track incoming backlinks from mentions to your website as part of PR measurement and SEO performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use backlink counts to show PR’s contribution to SEO; Prowly provides backlink tracking as part of monitoring, saving the cost of dedicated SEO tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: User-defined metrics specific to campaign objectives that you can add to dashboards and reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create and add custom metrics relevant to your goals so dashboards and reports reflect what matters most to your stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement type
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize mentions by engagement behaviors (shares, comments, reactions) to understand audience interaction with coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use engagement type to assess the qualitative impact of mentions beyond raw reach or counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filters for monitoring (keyword combinations, context, topic, site, reach, region, language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply filters such as keyword combinations & context, topic and website (1000+ combinations), estimated mention reach, region and language, and many others to surface only relevant results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set precise filters per campaign to reduce noise; large brands should expect irrelevant results without filtering. Tailor filters to campaign terms, industry context, and geography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom dashboards and tailored reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Create fully custom dashboards with chosen metrics, filters and chart types; build different dashboards for PR teams, CMOs, and company management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design reports for specific audiences so metrics and narratives match stakeholder needs. Ideally, monitoring tools should plug into reporting to create reports in minutes rather than hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alerts and spike detection (email digests, instant alerts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up recurring summaries, digests, and instant alerts (including spike alerts) for top mentions and for situations when tracked terms get a lot of mentions in a short time, especially negative spikes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alerts to receive only the relevant updates and to be notified immediately when crisis indicators (e.g., negative sentiment spikes) arise so you can act quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media monitoring vs broadcast/print monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Include digital media monitoring as well as broadcast monitoring (TV, radio, podcasts) and print monitoring (newspapers, magazines, journals) to avoid missing insights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine digital and traditional media coverage in one strategy to evaluate media investments and campaign ROI comprehensively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social listening (qualitative insights beyond counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social listening extends monitoring by analyzing qualitative metrics — sentiment, context, and overall social trends — to understand perception, not just counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use social listening to demonstrate PR value through qualitative impact on business performance; integrate social monitoring data into listening to avoid manual work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine AI-driven analysis with human oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage AI to analyze context, sentiment, and many properties of mentions, but 'combine data science with a human touch (and never rely on tools alone for sentiment analysis)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AI to scale detection and classification, but validate and adjust sentiment and context with human review to avoid automation errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark results against competitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Track both your brand and competitors' brand sentiment and metrics to benchmark performance over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use competitor benchmarking to contextualize results and set realistic targets for Share of Voice, sentiment, and visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis detection and prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Spot and prevent crises by monitoring for increased mentions with negative sentiment and using spike alerts to 'nip the blooming crisis in the bud.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set thresholds for negative sentiment and spike detection; ensure alerting routes to the right people so PR measures can be taken immediately.
